purpose: Alternative static DTC priority baseline for controlled comparison
important_scope: These are benchmark priority classes, not OEM severity values, safety ratings, repair instructions, or universal vehicle-independent urgency levels.
SAE J2012 defines standardized DTCs and descriptions; it does not establish the numeric priority scores used here.
Diagnostic urgency depends on vehicle, powertrain, calibration, fault status, symptoms, warning indicators, and manufacturer-specific fail-safe behavior.
Class assignments represent a broad potential-consequence rubric. They should be interpreted as a transparent experiment design choice, not a validated repair triage policy.

class_rubric.class_3: Potential for immediate operational impairment, loss of an important vehicle function, or significant secondary damage in applicable implementations.
class_rubric.class_2: Potential to affect engine/throttle control, feedback control, drivability, or emissions/fuel control; urgency is condition-dependent.
class_rubric.class_1: Typically associated with temperature-regulation/monitor behavior and often lower immediate operational impact, while still requiring vehicle-specific assessment.

dtcs.reason: Crankshaft-position signal faults can compromise engine-speed/position information and may cause no-start or engine operation issues in applicable vehicles.
dtcs.evidence_scope: generic functional consequence; exact symptom and fail-safe are OEM-specific

dtcs.reason: A sufficiently severe misfire can impair operation and may overheat or damage the catalytic converter; severity depends on misfire rate and operating conditions.
dtcs.evidence_scope: OEM service information documents conditional catalyst risk; not every P0300 has the same severity

dtcs.reason: A wheel-speed sensor fault may affect ABS/traction/stability functions in applicable chassis implementations.
dtcs.evidence_scope: system-function risk; affected features and fallback behavior vary by vehicle

dtcs.reason: Throttle-position performance/plausibility fault can affect engine torque control or invoke reduced-power behavior.
dtcs.evidence_scope: OEM-specific reduced-power/limp strategy can make this more urgent than this generic class suggests

dtcs.reason: Oxygen-sensor circuit fault can affect feedback-control diagnosis and emissions behavior.
dtcs.evidence_scope: fault subtype and operating state matter; code alone does not establish sensor failure or severity

dtcs.reason: System-too-lean condition may reflect air/fuel control deviation and can affect drivability or emissions.
dtcs.evidence_scope: cause and consequence depend on operating conditions and the underlying fault

dtcs.reason: System-too-rich condition may reflect air/fuel control deviation and can affect drivability, fuel use, or emissions.
dtcs.evidence_scope: cause and consequence depend on operating conditions and the underlying fault

dtcs.reason: Coolant-temperature-regulation fault is often associated with warm-up, operating-temperature, fuel-economy, or emissions effects.
dtcs.evidence_scope: not categorically low risk; overheating or other symptoms require separate assessment
